outcome: Third or fourth degree laceration rate
Neonatal intensive care unit admission rate
cohort: 18,214 women with live, term, singleton, vertex deliveries at one hospital from 2011 to 2015
finding: While solo obstetricians had a higher cesarean delivery rate, they also had lower rates of shoulder dystocia, third/fourth degree lacerations, and neonatal intensive care unit admissions, indicating a more conservative approach to labor management.
mod_finding: Solo obstetricians had a significantly higher rate of cesarean delivery compared to group obstetricians.
